summary:
All three St. Brigid discharges are reconciled under RBC-TOC-02. Each has a progress note, plus an addendum for decisions that changed when new items arrived while I worked.

WALTER KIM (pt-0005):
- Furosemide: changed from 20 mg daily to 40 mg twice daily (mr-t0001). The signed addendum (doc-00009) overrides the summary's 40 mg daily.
- Potassium chloride: stopped (mr-00076), as the discharge summary says.
- Omeprazole: kept (mr-00069). Pantoprazole was only the hospital's formulary substitute, so I didn't order it.
- Metoprolol XL, atorvastatin, aspirin: no change.
- Lisinopril: at first I kept it held because potassium was 5.4 on 10/21, and I made you a task (task-t0003). A repeat BMP on 10/23 showed K 4.7 and creatinine 1.21. That meets the discharge condition (creatinine below 1.5), so I resumed lisinopril 10 mg daily (mr-00072).
- Flags for you: task-t0003 no longer needs action, but the system wouldn't let me cancel it, so please close it. An unsigned draft addendum (doc-00902) proposes furosemide 60 mg twice daily. I didn't act on it because it isn't signed. You may want to check with St. Brigid. I sent you a message about both (comm-t0018).

TERENCE STARK (pt-0004):
- Carvedilol: I raised it to 12.5 mg twice daily per the discharge summary. A signed addendum then arrived (doc-00904): his heart rate was 48–52 with lightheadedness, and the increase was reversed before discharge. I put it back to 6.25 mg twice daily (mr-t0013).
- Aspirin and insulin 70/30 18 units twice daily: no change.
- Flag: atorvastatin 80 mg was continued at discharge, but his fills cover only about 24% of the 180 days before admission. Under the policy I made no change; please address adherence (message comm-t0006). His LDL was 134 on 10/08.
- Flag: he has been filling glipizide 5 mg from Dr. Desai at an outside pharmacy, with no clinic order. The discharge summary doesn't mention it, so I didn't order or change it. Please decide whether he should take it alongside insulin, given hypoglycemia risk and CKD stage 3 (message comm-t0007).

EARNEST ROBERTS (pt-0044):
- Insulin glargine, insulin lispro, rosuvastatin: no change.
- Lisinopril: I resumed it because creatinine was 1.08 and potassium 4.6 on 10/22. A new potassium of 5.5 then arrived (collected 10/23), so I put it back on hold (mr-00373).
- Flag: I made you an urgent task (task-t0014, due 10/26) to review his next potassium. He may need to be told not to restart lisinopril, since it was briefly active this morning.

I closed the four inbox items that arrived during the work, linking each to the action taken. The queues have nothing else new for these three patients.

Riverbend Pharmacy fill history (doc-00006) shows atorvastatin fills only on 12/03/2025 and 03/04/2026 (90-day supplies), covering about 44 of the 180 days before admission (~24%, below 80%).
